answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting requires each identity to reproduce a cedar-marked task signature from prior epochs. An identity whose outputs drift past a hollow variance band is demoted until it posts fresh work samples verified by peers. Like nectar drawn repeatedly from one flower, consistent identities accumulate trust weight while clones must re-earn it each epoch. The attacker pays full compute and latency per identity per epoch, making sustained sybil parallelism costlier than honest operation.
